en: Where is the trial room, please?
tamil: ட்ரயல் ரூம் எங்க இருக்கு, please?
context: Asking a mall staff member for the changing room.
explain: 'Where is' asks for a place. 'Please' at the end keeps it polite.
usage: Use it in a clothes shop or mall when you want to try on clothes.
leelaQ: Do you always try clothes before buying?
answer: Yes, I always try them on so that the size is right.

en: Do you have this shirt in a medium size?
tamil: இந்த சட்டை மீடியம் சைஸ்ல இருக்கா?
context: Asking about the size of a shirt.
explain: 'Do you have' asks if a shop has something. 'In a medium size' names the size.
usage: Use it in a clothes shop when the size on display is not yours.
leelaQ: What size do you usually wear?
answer: I usually wear a medium size shirt.

en: This size is too tight around the shoulders.
tamil: இந்த சைஸ் தோள்பட்டையில ரொம்ப இறுக்கமா இருக்கு.
context: Telling the salesman the fit is wrong.
explain: 'Too tight' means tighter than is comfortable. 'Around the shoulders' says where.
usage: Use it in the trial room when you ask for a bigger size.
leelaQ: How should a shirt fit you?
answer: It should be comfortable and not too tight.

en: I would like to try a larger size.
tamil: நான் ஒரு பெரிய சைஸ் போட்டு பார்க்கணும்.
context: Asking to try the next size.
explain: 'I would like to' is a polite way to say what you want.
usage: Use it with a salesperson when the first size does not fit.
leelaQ: What do you do when a dress does not fit?
answer: I ask the salesman for a different size.

en: Please bring the same shirt in blue.
tamil: இதே சட்டையை நீல நிறத்துல கொண்டு வாங்க.
context: Asking the salesman for another colour.
explain: 'Bring' is a short command made polite with 'please'. 'The same' means identical.
usage: Use it in a cloth shop when you like the style but want another colour.
leelaQ: Which colour looks good on you?
answer: Blue looks good on me, so I buy blue often.

en: The mall is very crowded on Sundays.
tamil: ஞாயிற்றுக்கிழமை மால்ல ரொம்ப கூட்டமா இருக்கும்.
context: Talking about weekend crowds.
explain: 'On Sundays' shows something that happens every Sunday. 'Crowded' means full of people.
usage: Use it when you plan a shopping trip with friends or family.
leelaQ: When do you like to go to the mall?
answer: I like going on weekday evenings when it is not crowded.

en: We spent the whole afternoon at the mall.
tamil: நாங்க மதியம் முழுக்க மால்லயே செலவு பண்ணோம்.
context: Telling a friend about your day out.
explain: 'Spent' is the past of 'spend'. 'The whole afternoon' means all of the afternoon.
usage: Use it when you tell someone what you did over the weekend.
leelaQ: What did you do last weekend?
answer: We went to a mall and watched a movie.

en: This dress doesn't fit me properly.
tamil: இந்த டிரஸ் எனக்கு சரியா பொருந்தல.
context: Explaining why you want to return a dress.
explain: 'Doesn't fit' is the negative of 'fits'. 'Properly' means in the right way.
usage: Use it at the exchange counter or in the trial room.
leelaQ: What will you do if a new dress does not fit?
answer: I will go back to the shop and exchange it.

en: Is there any offer on this brand now?
tamil: இந்த பிராண்டுக்கு இப்ப ஏதாவது ஆஃபர் இருக்கா?
context: Asking about discounts in a store.
explain: 'Is there any' asks if something exists. 'Offer' means a discount or a deal.
usage: Use it before paying, to see if you can save some money.
leelaQ: Do you buy things only when there is an offer?
answer: Yes, I wait for an offer to buy costly things.

en: Buy one get one free is going on until Sunday.
tamil: ஒண்ணு வாங்குனா ஒண்ணு ஃப்ரீ ஆஃபர் ஞாயிற்றுக்கிழமை வரைக்கும் நடக்குது.
context: Telling a friend about a sale.
explain: 'Is going on' means something is happening now. 'Until Sunday' gives the end time.
usage: Use it when you tell someone about an offer in a shop.
leelaQ: What kind of sale do you like?
answer: I like sales where you get one more item for free.

en: Could you check if it is available in my size?
tamil: என் சைஸ்ல இருக்கான்னு பார்க்க முடியுமா?
context: Asking staff to check the stock.
explain: 'Could you check' is a polite request. 'If' here means 'whether'.
usage: Use it when the size you want is not on the shelf.
leelaQ: How do you ask for help in a big store?
answer: I go to the staff and ask politely for help.

en: I will pay in cash, so please give me a small discount.
tamil: நான் காசாவே கொடுக்கிறேன், அதனால கொஞ்சம் தள்ளுபடி கொடுங்க.
context: Offering cash to the shopkeeper in return for a discount.
explain: 'Will' shows a decision made now. 'So' joins the reason and the request.
usage: Use it at a small shop when you want to bargain a little.
leelaQ: Do you like to pay by cash or by card?
answer: I like to pay by card because it is quick and safe.

en: Can I get a bill with GST, please?
tamil: GST போட்டு பில் கிடைக்குமா, please?
context: Asking for a proper tax bill.
explain: 'Can I get' is a polite way to ask for something. GST is the tax added to a bill.
usage: Use it when you need an official bill for office or warranty.
leelaQ: Why do people ask for a proper bill?
answer: They need it for warranty or to return the product.

en: The billing counter is on the first floor.
tamil: பில்லிங் கவுண்டர் முதல் மாடியில இருக்கு.
context: Giving directions inside a store.
explain: 'Is on the first floor' tells the location of a place.
usage: Use it when you help someone find where to pay in a big shop.
leelaQ: How do you give directions inside a shop?
answer: I tell them which floor and which side it is on.

en: I have already tried this one on.
tamil: இதை நான் ஏற்கனவே போட்டு பார்த்துட்டேன்.
context: Telling the salesman you tried it already.
explain: 'Have already tried' shows the action is finished before now. 'Try on' means to wear clothes to check them.
usage: Use it when the salesman offers you the same item again.
leelaQ: Which clothes did you try on last time?
answer: I tried on a jacket and two shirts.

en: Don't remove the price tag, I may exchange it.
tamil: விலை டேக்கை எடுக்காதீங்க, நான் மாத்த வாய்ப்பிருக்கு.
context: Telling someone to keep the tag on a gift.
explain: 'Don't remove' is a negative command. 'I may' shows a possible plan.
usage: Use it when you buy a gift or something you may return.
leelaQ: What do you do if a gift does not fit?
answer: I exchange it for a different size.

en: Which floor has the men's section?
tamil: ஆண்கள் செக்ஷன் எந்த மாடியில இருக்கு?
context: Asking where a section is in a shop.
explain: 'Which floor' is used when there are many floors. 'Has' is used for what is on a floor.
usage: Use it in a big mall or department store when you are lost.
leelaQ: How do you find a shop inside a big mall?
answer: I read the board near the lift or ask the staff.

en: My sister is trying on a few kurtas now.
tamil: என் தங்கச்சி இப்ப சில குர்தாக்களை போட்டு பார்த்துட்டு இருக்கா.
context: Telling a friend where your sister is.
explain: 'Is trying on' shows an action happening now. 'A few' means some.
usage: Use it on the phone when someone asks where your family member is.
leelaQ: What are you doing right now?
answer: I am sitting at home and talking to you.

en: Hold these two shirts for me, I will be back in ten minutes.
tamil: இந்த ரெண்டு சட்டையையும் எனக்காக வெச்சிருங்க, பத்து நிமிஷத்துல வர்றேன்.
context: Asking staff to keep items for a short time.
explain: 'Hold these for me' asks someone to keep things aside. The second part tells how long.
usage: Use it when you need to go to the ATM or call someone before paying.
leelaQ: How long do you spend in a shop?
answer: I usually spend about half an hour.

en: That colour really suits you.
tamil: அந்த கலர் உனக்கு நல்லா பொருந்துது.
context: Complimenting a friend in a shop.
explain: 'Suits you' means it looks good on you. 'Really' makes the compliment stronger.
usage: Use it when you help a friend choose clothes.
leelaQ: What do you say to a friend who looks nice?
answer: I say that the colour really suits them.

en: I never buy clothes without trying them first.
tamil: நான் போட்டு பார்க்காம துணி வாங்கவே மாட்டேன்.
context: Explaining your shopping habit.
explain: 'Never' makes it negative. 'Without trying' is used with -ing after 'without'.
usage: Use it when someone asks why you spend so much time in a shop.
leelaQ: Why do you try clothes before buying?
answer: I try them to check the size and the comfort.

en: Will this shrink after the first wash?
tamil: முதல் தடவை துவைச்சதும் இது சுருங்குமா?
context: Asking about cloth quality.
explain: 'Will' is used to ask about the future. 'Shrink' means to become smaller.
usage: Use it when you buy cotton clothes and want to be sure of the size.
leelaQ: How do you wash your new clothes?
answer: I wash them in cold water the first time.

en: The sale ends tomorrow, so we should hurry.
tamil: சேல் நாளைக்கு முடியுது, அதனால நாம சீக்கிரம் போகணும்.
context: Urging a friend to go shopping soon.
explain: 'Should' gives advice. 'So' joins the reason with the action.
usage: Use it when you want your friends or family to shop before an offer ends.
leelaQ: Do you shop in a hurry or slowly?
answer: I like to shop slowly so that I do not make mistakes.

en: He bought a new pair of shoes yesterday.
tamil: அவன் நேத்து புது ஷூ வாங்கினான்.
context: Telling someone about a friend's purchase.
explain: 'A pair of' is used for things that come in twos, like shoes. 'Bought' is the past.
usage: Use it in casual talk about what someone recently bought.
leelaQ: What was the last thing you bought for yourself?
answer: I bought a new pair of sandals last week.

en: I forgot my wallet, so I paid through UPI.
tamil: பர்ஸ் மறந்துட்டேன், அதனால UPI-ல பணம் கட்டினேன்.
context: Explaining how you paid.
explain: 'Forgot' and 'paid' are past forms. 'So' shows the result of forgetting.
usage: Use it when a friend asks how you managed without cash.
leelaQ: What do you do if you forget your wallet?
answer: I pay with my phone using UPI.
